faqs.answer: A garment sourcing agent, also called a buying office or buying house, represents overseas brands in Bangladesh. ABD Sourcing Bangladesh matches your product to a suitable partner factory and manages development, costing, sampling, quality control, production follow-up and shipment, giving you one accountable team in Dhaka instead of several factory contacts.

faqs.question: Is ABD Sourcing Bangladesh a factory or a buying office?

Every order also passes a seven-step quality control process, from fabric inspection to final shipment approval, before goods ship.

faqs.question: Which certifications do ABD's partner factories hold?
faqs.answer: BSCI (Business Social Compliance Initiative), SEDEX (Supplier Ethical Data Exchange), WRAP (Worldwide Responsible Accredited Production), ISO, OEKO-TEX, GOTS (Global Organic Textile Standard), GRS (Global Recycled Standard), SA 8000:2014, Fairtrade, RCS (Recycled Claim Standard) and Recycled OEKO-TEX are held across our partner factories. Tell us which one your programme requires and we match the order.

faqs.question: What is a BSCI audit?
faqs.answer: BSCI, the Business Social Compliance Initiative run by amfori, assesses working conditions in supplier factories against a code of conduct covering areas such as fair remuneration, working hours, health and safety, and no child or bonded labour. The audit result shows how closely a factory meets that code.

faqs.question: What are SEDEX and SMETA?
faqs.answer: Sedex, the Supplier Ethical Data Exchange, is an online platform where suppliers share responsible-sourcing data with buyers. SMETA is the audit methodology commonly used with it, assessing labour standards and health and safety, with environment and business ethics in the four-pillar version. Factories can share audit results with customers.

faqs.question: What is WRAP certification?
faqs.answer: WRAP, Worldwide Responsible Accredited Production, certifies that a sewn-products factory follows a set of social compliance principles covering areas such as forced labour, child labour, working hours, health and safety and environment, verified by independent audit. It is widely used for apparel factories.

faqs.question: What is the difference between GOTS, GRS and OEKO-TEX?
faqs.answer: GOTS certifies organic fibre content plus environmental and social criteria through processing. GRS verifies recycled content and chain of custody. OEKO-TEX Standard 100 tests finished textiles for harmful substances. They answer different questions, so a programme may need one or several; all three are held across our partner factories.

faqs.question: What are SA 8000, Fairtrade and RCS?
faqs.answer: SA 8000 is Social Accountability International's workplace standard covering child and forced labour, working hours, pay and health and safety. Fairtrade sets social, economic and environmental standards for producers and supply chains. RCS, the Recycled Claim Standard from Textile Exchange, verifies recycled content and tracks it through the supply chain.

faqs.question: How is factory certification different from ABD's quality control?
faqs.answer: Certification shows a factory meets social, environmental or product-safety standards, but it does not check your specific order. ABD's seven-step QC does: fabric inspection, PP sample approval, inline, mid-line, final random and packing inspection, then shipment approval, so each order is verified against your specification.

faqs.question: What fabrics are used for heavyweight workwear hoodies?

faqs.question: How is workwear quality controlled?

product-development.answer: ABD Sourcing Bangladesh provides apparel product development in Bangladesh, turning a tech pack, sketch or reference garment into a production-ready sample. It briefs the partner factory's sample room directly, runs fit, proto and SMS sample rounds, and manages counter-sample and sealed-sample approval so the first physical sample lands close to the buyer's intent.

faqs.question: What is a tech pack and do I need one to start?
faqs.answer: A tech pack is the specification document for a garment: sketches, measurements, materials, construction details, trims and labels. It is a good starting point, but ABD can also work from a sketch or a reference garment and turn it into a production-ready sample with the partner factory's sample room.

faqs.question: How does ABD turn a reference garment into a sample?
faqs.answer: We brief the factory sample room directly, track every sample round to closure, and ship each sample with measurement and fabric notes so your feedback is unambiguous. We also flag cost or feasibility risks early, before the style reaches bulk production, so the first sample lands close to your intent.

faqs.question: Which sample rounds does product development include?
faqs.answer: Development covers fit, proto and SMS sample rounds, print, embroidery and wash development, and counter-sample and sealed-sample management. A sealed sample is the final approved reference that bulk production must match, so the factory, our QC team and you all work to the same standard.

faqs.question: Can ABD develop garments in organic cotton or recycled fabrics?
faqs.answer: Yes. We develop knit and woven styles in combed cotton, organic cotton and recycled blends, including recycled polyester for performance wear, to suit each market's compliance profile. faqs.question: Can you help with fabric and trim development during sampling?
faqs.answer: Yes. Fabric and trim development with mill options is part of product development, alongside lab-dip shade approval through our material sourcing service. faqs.question: What does fabric and trims sourcing include?
faqs.answer: It covers knit and woven fabric sourced to your target GSM and composition, yarn, and full trim packages such as labels, zippers, drawcords, buttons and packaging. We compare material costs across suppliers and approve shade and hand feel against a physical standard before bulk, using a vetted base of Bangladeshi and regional mills.

faqs.question: Can ABD source organic, recycled or certified fabrics?
faqs.answer: Yes. We source recycled, organic and OEKO-TEX, GOTS or GRS certified inputs, and match composition and certification to your market's compliance needs. Share the certification your programme requires and we confirm the fabric route with the partner factory before development starts.

faqs.question: What is a lab dip?
faqs.answer: A lab dip is a small piece of fabric dyed in a laboratory to match a colour standard, so you can approve the shade before bulk dyeing. ABD manages lab-dip and bulk-dye shade approval against a physical standard, which protects colour consistency between the sealed sample and production.

faqs.question: How does ABD keep fabric deliveries on schedule?
faqs.answer: We hold suppliers to delivery dates that protect the production calendar. Every milestone, including fabric arrival, is tracked against the time-and-action plan managed by your merchandiser, so slippage surfaces early and you can decide how to respond before the ship date is at risk.

faqs.question: How do you compare material prices?
faqs.answer: We run a material cost comparison across suppliers for the same GSM, composition and certification, so you can see the price difference between options before committing. Combined with target-cost negotiation from merchandising, this helps settle the right quality at the right price point before the order is placed.

faqs.question: What does a garment merchandiser do for my order?
faqs.answer: Your merchandiser is the day-to-day contact on the ground. They manage open-cost and target-cost negotiation, order placement and PO management, time-and-action planning, sample tracking and approval follow-up, and daily order-status reporting, keeping you confident the order is on track from costing to the confirmed shipment date.

faqs.question: Will I have a single point of contact at ABD?
faqs.answer: Yes. One merchandiser owns your account end to end, with no handoffs and no lost context. We work to your time zone and reply quickly in clear English, so questions on samples, costing or shipment dates get answered without waiting for a factory to respond.

faqs.question: What is a time-and-action (T&A) calendar?
faqs.answer: A time-and-action calendar, also called a critical path, lists every milestone of an order with its due date: approvals, fabric arrival, cutting, sewing, inspection and shipment. ABD tracks each milestone against the T&A so slippage surfaces early and the buyer can decide on corrective action before the ship date is at risk.

faqs.question: How does ABD handle costing and price negotiation?
faqs.answer: We negotiate open-cost and target-cost structures with the partner factory and compare material costs across suppliers. Costing sits early in our production flow, after development and before order confirmation, so you approve a clear price for the agreed specification before any bulk order is placed.

faqs.question: How often will I receive order updates?
faqs.answer: Merchandising includes daily order-status reporting to the buyer, with sample tracking and approval follow-up throughout. Each milestone is tracked against the time-and-action plan, so you can see real progress on samples, materials, production and shipment without having to chase the factory.

seo.metaTitle: Garment Quality Control Bangladesh | ABD Sourcing
seo.metaDescription: Seven-step garment QC from fabric inspection to AQL final random inspection and shipment approval, run on every order. Request a quote from ABD.
seo.heading: Garment Quality Control in Bangladesh: A 7-Step Inspection Process

quality-assurance.answer: ABD Sourcing Bangladesh runs garment quality control in Bangladesh in seven steps on every order: fabric inspection, pre-production sample approval, inline inspection, mid-line inspection, AQL-based final random inspection, packing inspection and shipment approval. Shipment is released only after every gate passes, with inspections documented with photos for the buyer.

faqs.question: What is ABD Sourcing Bangladesh's quality control process?
faqs.answer: Our QC team runs seven steps on every order: fabric inspection, PP sample approval, inline inspection, mid-line inspection, final random inspection, packing inspection and shipment approval. Each gate must pass before the next, so problems are caught while they are still cheap to fix rather than after goods are packed.

faqs.question: What is AQL inspection?
faqs.answer: AQL, the Acceptable Quality Limit, is a sampling standard used in final inspection: a set number of units is checked from the finished batch, and the lot passes only if defects stay within the agreed limit. ABD performs an AQL-based final random inspection on finished, packed goods before shipment approval.

faqs.question: What is a pre-production (PP) sample approval?
faqs.answer: A pre-production sample is made before bulk production starts, using the approved materials and trims. ABD signs it off against the approved specification, trims and measurements, so bulk production begins against a confirmed reference that you and the factory have both agreed.

faqs.question: Do you inspect during production or only at the end?
faqs.answer: During production. Inline inspection audits the sewing lines to catch construction issues early, and a mid-line inspection confirms the run stays within tolerance as volume scales. Incoming fabric is also checked for shade, GSM, width and defects before cutting, in addition to the final random inspection.

faqs.question: When is a shipment approved for release?
faqs.answer: Shipment approval is the seventh and last gate. Final clearance is issued only when every earlier gate has passed: fabric, PP sample, inline, mid-line, final random and packing inspection. Shipment is released only after every gate passes, so the buyer receives goods that met the agreed process.

faqs.question: Will I receive inspection reports?
faqs.answer: Our inspections are AQL-based and documented with photos for the buyer, so you can see what was checked and what was found. Packing inspection also verifies cartons, polybags, labelling and assortment against the packing list before shipment approval is issued.

seo.heading: Garment Production Monitoring in Bangladesh

production-monitoring.answer: ABD Sourcing Bangladesh provides garment production monitoring in Bangladesh, checking bulk production at the factory floor against the agreed plan. It confirms line loading and capacity, tracks daily or weekly output, flags bottlenecks, follows finishing and packing, and escalates risks to the ship date to the buyer with a recovery plan.

faqs.question: How does ABD monitor garment production in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: We monitor bulk production at the factory floor against the agreed plan, from line loading to finishing. That means confirming line loading and capacity, tracking daily or weekly output versus plan, flagging bottlenecks, and following finishing and packing progress to keep the order moving toward its confirmed shipment date.

faqs.question: What happens if production falls behind schedule?
faqs.answer: Risks to the ship date are escalated to the buyer with a recovery plan. Because we track real output on the floor rather than relying on factory promises, delays and bottlenecks surface early, so the buyer can decide on the recovery options while there is still time to act.

faqs.question: Do you check factory capacity before an order starts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Production monitoring begins with line-loading and capacity confirmation, so the order is planned against real capacity at the partner factory. We then track daily or weekly output against that plan and report real output to the buyer, not just factory promises.

faqs.question: How is production monitoring different from quality inspection?
faqs.answer: Monitoring tracks quantity and timing: whether output is on plan for the confirmed ship date. Quality inspection checks whether the goods meet the specification, through our seven-step QC process. ABD runs both, so you see schedule risks and quality risks before shipment.

faqs.question: Do you manage finishing and packing progress?
faqs.answer: Yes. We coordinate finishing and packing so nothing stalls at the last step, tracking progress alongside sewing output so the order keeps moving toward its confirmed shipment date. Packing inspection then verifies cartons, polybags, labelling and assortment against the packing list before shipment approval is issued.

faqs.question: Do you verify cartons and shipping marks?
